level_1: Acquires a foundational history for common infectious diseases and syndromes
Performs an examination that elicits uncommon or complicated infectious diseases and syndromes
level_2: Performs a foundational physical examination
Acquires a tailored history that incorporates epidemiology, past clinical data, and nuances specific for suspected pathogens or syndromes
level_3: Acquires a complete history, including specific host and environmental factors
Performs a tailored examination that elicits subtle findings of infectious diseases and syndromes
level_4: Performs an examination that elicits common or straightforward infectious diseases and syndromes
Serves as a role model in obtaining a history that identifies subtle details and resolves ambiguity in the patient history
level_5: Acquires a detailed history incorporating pertinent supplemental information
Serves as a role model who has mastered the art of examination that helps in making a definitive diagnosis

subcompetencies.name: Management of Patients with Possible and Proven Infectious Diseases

level_1: Develops an initial assessment for patients with low-complexity conditions
level_2: Develops initial and follow-up management plans for patients with low-complexity conditions
level_3: Develops an initial and follow-up plan for patients with moderate-complexity conditions and adjusts the plan over the course of clinical care
level_4: Develops a comprehensive management plan, including contingency plans for patients with complex conditions
level_5: Develops customized management plans for all patients, regardless of the complexity of the condition, and incorporating diagnostic uncertainty and cost effectiveness

level_1: Respectfully responds to a consultation request and conveys recommendations, with supervision
Prioritizes workflow in response to consult acuity and urgency
level_2: Recognizes consult acuity and urgency, with supervision
Provides comprehensive and prioritized recommendations, including assessment and rationale to all necessary health care team members
level_3: Identifies and clarifies the clinical questions and recommendations for the consultation
Mobilizes resources to provide care in an urgent situation
level_4: Recognizes consult acuity and urgency independently
Leads the health care team in the provision of effective consultative services across the spectrum of disease complexity and acuity
level_5: Seeks and integrates input from different members of the health care team and provides recommendations to the primary team in a clear and timely manner

level_1: Integrates patient- specific information to generate a limited differential diagnosis
level_2: Provides a limited prioritized differential diagnosis using supporting rationale
level_3: Formulates a prioritized differential diagnosis; demonstrates the ability to modify a diagnosis based on a patient’s clinical course and additional data
level_4: Formulates a differential diagnosis to include atypical presentations and uncommon disorders; recognizes sources of diagnostic error
level_5: Formulates a differential diagnosis to include newly recognized and emerging conditions

level_1: Demonstrates foundational knowledge of diagnostic evaluation for pathogens
Applies diagnostic testing in consideration of risks, benefits, and consequences for clinical syndromes
level_2: Demonstrates foundational knowledge of diagnostic evaluation for clinical syndromes
Interprets diagnostic evaluations for pathogens and clinical syndromes, considering performance characteristics, limitations, and nuances
level_3: Applies knowledge of diagnostic evaluation for common pathogens
Teaches others the nuances of directed diagnostic evaluation for pathogens and clinical syndromes
level_4: Applies knowledge of indications for diagnostic evaluation for common clinical syndromes
level_5: Applies knowledge of indications for diagnostic evaluation of uncommon pathogens, antimicrobial resistance, and therapeutic drug monitoring

subcompetencies.name: Treatment and Therapeutics including Anti-Infectives, Immunoprophylaxis, and Adjunctive Therapies

level_1: Demonstrates foundational knowledge of common anti- infectives, including spectrum of activity, contraindications, and clinical indications
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of common anti-infectives, immunoprophylaxis, and adjunctive therapies, including dosing, monitoring, and adverse effects
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of common anti-infectives, immunoprophylaxis, and adjunctive therapies, including resistance mechanisms, drug interactions, and relative effectiveness
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of uncommon anti- infectives, immunoprophylaxis, and adjunctive therapies, including dosing, monitoring, resistance mechanisms, drug interactions, adverse effects, and relative effectiveness
level_5: Teaches others the nuances of anti-infectives, immunoprophylaxis, and adjunctive therapies

subcompetencies.name: Infection Control/Prevention, Antimicrobial Stewardship, and Epidemiology

level_1: Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the principles of infection prevention
Implements infection prevention measures for uncommon situations
Teaches on the epidemiological impact of infectious diseases on population health
level_2: Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the principles of antimicrobial stewardship
Implements antimicrobial stewardship practices for uncommon situations
Demonstrates innovation and leadership in infection prevention practices
level_3: Implements infection prevention measures for common situations
Practices the basic principles of epidemiology, including identifying and responding to common epidemiological events
Demonstrates innovation and leadership in antimicrobial stewardship practices
level_4: Implements antimicrobial stewardship practices for common situations
Teaches infection prevention practices to health care providers, patients, and the medical community
Leads a team in identifying and responding to epidemiological events
level_5: Demonstrates basic knowledge of the principles of epidemiology
Teaches health care providers, patients, and the medical community antimicrobial stewardship practices

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of pathophysiological and foundational science pertaining to common infectious diseases and host response
level_2: Demonstrates advanced knowledge of pathophysiological and foundational science concepts pertaining to common infectious diseases and host response
level_3: Applies advanced knowledge of pathophysiological and foundational science concepts pertaining to common infectious diseases and host response
level_4: Applies advanced knowledge of pathophysiological and foundational science concepts pertaining to uncommon infectious diseases and host response
level_5: Applies comprehensive knowledge of pathophysiology and foundational science pertaining to new and emerging infectious diseases and issues of host response

level_1: Identifies areas worthy of scholarly activity
level_2: Plans a scholarly activity 	Implements scholarly activity
level_3: Disseminates independent scholarly work, locally or regionally, that has generated new medical knowledge, educational programs, or process improvement
level_4: Disseminates independent scholarly work, nationally or internationally, that has generated new medical knowledge, educational programs, or process improvement

level_1: Identifies patient safety events and discloses them to leadership, patients, and/or patients’ family members
Participates in efforts to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Leads efforts to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_3: Analyzes the factors that contribute to patient safety events
level_4: Reports patient safety events using the health system’s reporting mechanism
level_5: Offers prevention strategies to mitigate patient safety events

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of quality improvement methodologies and metrics
level_2: Identifies opportunities for quality improvement projects
level_3: Participates in quality improvement projects
level_4: Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_5: Leads quality improvement projects

level_1: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions and coordination of care and hand-offs
level_2: Performs safe and effective transitions and coordination of care and hand-offs in routine clinical situations
level_3: Performs safe and effective transitions and coordination of care/hand- offs in complex clinical situations
level_4: Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions and coordination of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems
level_5: Improves quality of transitions and coordination of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
level_2: Identifies specific population and community health needs for the local population
level_3: Identifies local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_4: Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_5: Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the health care system
Engages with patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment models
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Advocates for patient care needs with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model
level_4: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care
level_5: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system
Actively engaged in influencing health policy through advocacy activities at the local, regional, or national level

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence for patient care and elicits patient preferences and values to guide care
level_2: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient values and preferences, to the care of patients with common conditions
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient values and preference, to the care of patients with complex conditions
level_4: Critically appraises conflicting or ambiguous evidence to guide individualized patient care
level_5: Mentors others to critically appraise and apply evidence

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Identifies personal and professional development goals and recognizes gaps between expectations and actual performance
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
level_2: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Intentionally seeks performance data consistently with adaptability and humility, considering alternatives in narrowing the gaps between expectations and actual performance
level_3: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input), and analyzes and reflects on gaps to inform goals
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and improves it when necessary
level_4: Designs and implements a learning plan, with prompting
Role models commitment to self-improvement and coaches others on reflective practice
level_5: Seeks performance data episodically, with adaptability and humility, and institutes behavioral changes to narrow the gaps between expectations and actual performance
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others

level_1: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations
level_2: Identifies and describes potential personal triggers for professionalism lapses and takes responsibility for one’s own professionalism lapses
level_3: Demonstrates a pattern of professional behavior in complex or stressful situations; describes when and where to report professionalism lapses
level_4: Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
level_5: Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of ethical principles
level_2: Applies ethical principles to address straightforward situations
level_3: Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles and identifies the need to seek help in addressing complex situations
level_4: Uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed
level_5: Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Performs tasks and responsibilities with prompting
level_2: Recognizes factors that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner and describes strategies for improvement
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
level_4: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
level_5: Creates strategies to enhance others ability to complete administrative tasks and patient care efficiently

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
level_2: Lists available resources for personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional factors that positively and/or negatively affect well-being
level_3: Describes institutional resources that are meant to promote well-being
Creates institutional level interventions that promote colleagues’ well-being
level_4: With assistance, proposes a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional programs designed to examine systemic contributors to burnout
level_5: Recognizes which institutional factors affect well-being

level_1: Uses clear language and non-verbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
Adjusts communication strategies based on identified barriers, incorporating patient and caregiver expectations and goals of care
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication
Establishes and maintains therapeutic relationships using shared decision making, regardless of complexity
level_3: Establishes and maintains a therapeutic relationship with the patient using active listening and clear language in straightforward encounters
Proactively improves communication by addressing barriers and biases
level_4: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication
Serves as a role model in establishing respectful, culturally sensitive therapeutic relationships while mitigating communication barriers and engaging in critical self-reflection
level_5: Establishes and maintains a therapeutic relationship using effective communication behaviors in challenging patient encounters

level_1: Communicates information effectively in a manner that demonstrates respect for all members of the interprofessional team
level_2: Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team and adjusts communication approach to team needs, promoting open and safe communication
level_3: Facilitates interprofessional team communication to reconcile conflict and provides constructive feedback to team members
level_4: Leads and facilitates regular interdisciplinary discussions, including in complex and challenging situations
level_5: Models and coaches flexible communication strategies that facilitate excellence in interprofessional teamwork

level_1: Accurately documents comprehensive and current information
Independently selects direct and indirect forms of communication based on context
level_2: Communicates using formats specified by institutional policy to safeguard patient personal health information
Concisely documents clinical reasoning, including anticipatory guidance, while satisfying institutional billing needs and compliance
level_3: Documents encounter, including clinical reasoning in an organized manner
Models effective written and verbal communication
level_4: Selects direct and indirect forms of communication based on context, with guidance
Coaches others in accurately documenting diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning
level_5: Documents encounter through prioritized and concise yet thorough notes
Guides departmental or institutional communication policies and procedures
